questions.q: What is the difference between the scalar $s = 5$ and the 1D vector $v = [5]$?
options: They are exactly the same object, just written differently
The 1D vector holds two numbers, the scalar holds one
The scalar has a direction, the vector does not
The scalar is a single number (how much); the 1D vector is an arrow along one axis with a direction
questions.explain: Both hold one number, but the vector is treated as an arrow on a number line (left or right). Mixing up `5` and `[5]` is a classic shape bug in AI code.

questions.q: A 28×28 grayscale MNIST-style image is unrolled (flattened) for a basic neural network. How many dimensions does the resulting vector have?
questions.explain: Flattening stacks the 28 rows of 28 pixels end to end: $28 \times 28 = 784$ numbers, so the image becomes a 784-dimensional vector.

questions.q: Using the same idea, how long is the vector you get by flattening a 32×32 **colour** (RGB) image?
questions.explain: Each pixel has 3 channel values: $32 \times 32 \times 3 = 3072$. Forgetting the colour channels gives the trap answer 1024.

questions.q: Which vector has **no** direction, so the page draws it without an arrowhead?
questions.explain: Every non-zero vector points somewhere; only the zero vector has length 0 and therefore no direction.
